name: Titus
title: Paul's true child in the faith
summary: Titus was a Greek Christian who became one of the apostle Paul's most trusted coworkers and envoys. He played an important role in resolving conflicts in the church at Corinth and was later appointed as leader of the churches on Crete. Paul wrote a letter to him that is preserved as one of the Pastoral Epistles in the New Testament.

keyEvents.title: Participated in the apostolic council in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Titus traveled with Paul and Barnabas to Jerusalem to discuss the issue of circumcision for Gentile Christians. As an uncircumcised Greek, he became living proof that salvation is by faith alone.

keyEvents.title: Envoy to Corinth
keyEvents.description: Paul sent Titus to Corinth to handle conflicts in the church and organize the collection for the poor in Jerusalem. His mission was successful and brought joy to Paul.

keyEvents.title: Led the collection for Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Titus was entrusted with completing the collection for the saints in Jerusalem from the church in Corinth, and proved himself to be a zealous and reliable coworker.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Leader in Crete
keyEvents.description: Paul left Titus in Crete to set in order what was left and appoint elders in every town. This shows the great trust Paul had in him.

keyEvents.title: Received Guidance on Church Leadership
keyEvents.description: Paul wrote a letter to Titus with instructions on how he should choose leaders, handle false teaching, and teach the congregation about a godly life.

keyEvents.title: Planned Meeting in Nicopolis
keyEvents.description: Paul asked Titus to come to him in Nicopolis, which shows their close cooperation and friendship in ministry.
